text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition Socialists lost in Sunday's local elections after they committed a series of electoral mistakes, the newspaper said in an editorial.

- Pranvera Hoxha, daughter of the late communist dictator Enver Hoxha, complains to Albanian authorities and foreign embassies over the fate of her husband, Klement Kolaneci, recently arrested on suspected links with a guerilla group.
- Run-off round of local elections to be held for 19 city halls and 73 communes in Albania's south on Sunday.
- A delegation of the Council of Europe, monitoring Albania's local elections, said voting was mainly free and fair though it regretted some irregularities.
- Another monitoring group, the U.S. Republican Institute, also said Albania's local polls were free and fair despite some irregularities.
- Almost 40 percent of the Albanians did not take part in the elections.
- Some 54 percent of voters in the Benca prison in southern Albania, where opposition Socialist leader Fatos Nanos is serving a jail term, supported the opposition.
- About 1.87 million Albanians live in the countryside where living standards are still lower than in urban areas.
- Monthly average salaries have fallen to $36.5 for public sector employees and to $60 for private sector jobs, compared to about $65 last year.
- Tirana hospitals complain about lack of key medications.
- Opposition Socialists call on their supporters to participate in the run-off of local polls next Sunday despite a defeat in the first round.
- Soccer coach Sulejman Starova declined to accept an offer to take over Albania's under-21 national team.
- Annual inflation has been reduced to an expected 7.8 percent this year from as much as 226 percent in 1993.
